subject: COP z-sort DMA ($6FE) on Zero Team USA
reference: pristine MAME 0.289 zeroteam, read-only taps (sim/mame/sort_probe.lua, sim/mame/run_sort_probe.py)
observations: Every call uses sort_ram=0x4, lookup=0x8d6c, param=2 (descending).
Trigger data ranges 2..81. In all 3,908 calls the lookup entry at index `data` is a live, ascending table entry and the zero terminator sits at index data+1, so the live count is data+1.
MAME 0.289 dma_zsorting() sorts only `data` entries (leaves the last live object unsorted); this matches its raiden2.cpp TODO that zeroteam sort-DMA / sprite priorities are broken.
The key is the signed 32-bit dword at (sort_ram+val): low word at +0, high word (integer Y) at +2 (V30 little endian).
rtl_defect_found: Inherited donor sort read a single 16-bit word at (sort_ram+val)&~3 (the low/fraction word on this CPU) into a 60-entry register array. Replaying the observed tables through the production COP left the table unsorted in 597/604 cases.
rtl_fix: rtl/Raiden2/Raiden2_cop3.sv: RAM-backed stable insertion sort, 128 entries, signed 32-bit key {word@+2,word@+0}, n = data+1.
replay: sim/run_cop_sort.sh + sim/cop_sort_main.cpp: production COP vs stable signed-dword sort of the observed tables: 0 mismatches in 604 and 3304 cases (n=data would mismatch in 338 and 2870).
limits: Expected result is the MAME algorithm with n=data+1, derived from observed table structure; no PCB evidence. COP random-number source and undumped PALs remain unresolved.
